trial_court: Prl. Judge, Family Court, Tumakuru, M.C.No.27/2013
case_name: Sri. Sridharachari @ Sridhar vs Smt Suvarna
facts_of_case: Marriage of the appellant with the respondent was solemnized on 11.05.1986. The couple had lived together for about 16 years before the respondent left the company of the appellant and started residing with her parents. The appellant filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, praying to dissolve the marriage on the ground of desertion.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the appellant to prove that the respondent-wife was guilty of desertion without a valid reason for a continuous period of more than two years immediately prior to filing the petition.
legal_principles.held: The appellant who has approached the Family Court in a petition filed by him under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Act, was required to prove before the Family Court that the respondent-wife was guilty of deserting him without there being any valid reason for a continuous period of more than two years immediately prior to filing of the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The Family Court has to properly appreciate the oral and documentary evidence available on record before dismissing a petition.
legal_principles.held: He submits that the Family Court has erred in dismissing the petition and it has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dismissing the petition filed by the appellant-husband under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, is upheld.
